h1: 2026-10-15: EP=2 context sweep and phase-fenced overlap
p: Target: openai/gpt-oss-20b. Draft: zhuyksir/EAGLE3-gpt-oss-20b-bf16. Hardware: two NVIDIA H200 GPUs, approximately 141 GiB each, connected through NVLink (NV18). This follow-up retains the original plots above and adds a new controlled experiment.

The requested native TBO-on configurations cannot be measured in this checkout. With the working NCCL EP backend (moe-a2a-backend=none), enabling TBO is rejected during argument validation because that path requires attention DP. GPT-OSS has no native TBO operation path, and its DeepEP forward branch explicitly raises NotImplementedError. The custom target/draft schedule below is a separate experiment and is not labeled as native SGLang TBO.

The TBO support failures apply to the whole configuration; they do not represent 80 separately executed performance measurements. References: SGLang EP/TBO documentation; checkout validation; GPT-OSS DeepEP branch.

Batch sizes: 1, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256. Context budgets: 4k, 16k, 32k, 64k, 128k, where k=1024 tokens. The user removed 256k and 512k. Context means prompt plus generated output; at the native 128k boundary, six prompt positions are reserved consistently in every mode (four EAGLE draft-token slots plus two scheduler positions) to retain 128 generated tokens. Earlier boundary-clipped runs are kept only as diagnostics.

The draft checkpoint declares a 4096-token limit. With the user's explicit approval, runs above that limit use SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1. SGLang extends the draft's position-cache limit to 131072; its RoPE scaling is otherwise unchanged. The target remains within its native 131072-token limit. Longer-context draft results are experimental, and acceptance plus token-correctness checks are reported separately.

Common settings: TP=2, EP=2, FA3 attention, NCCL collectives, full decode CUDA graphs, prefill CUDA graphs disabled, memory fraction 0.8, sliding/full KV-cache ratio 0.1, chunked prefill 8192, maximum running requests 256, seed 42. Custom AllReduce, FlashInfer AllReduce fusion, and the CPU overlap scheduler are disabled consistently across compared modes. These settings isolate the scheduling comparison rather than represent an optimized default deployment. EAGLE3 uses 3 draft steps, top-k 1, and 4 verification tokens.

Each synthetic prompt has a distinct document prefix and repeated prose, ending in a summarization instruction. Each cell flushes the prefix cache, records one cold-request latency, warms the request again, and measures three unprofiled repetitions with greedy sampling and ignore_eos=True. Reported throughput is completed output tokens divided by HTTP request wall time with a cached prefix. It includes request transport and scheduling costs; it is not pure GPU-kernel throughput. Profiler captures are separate, cover eight scheduler steps, and retain both GPU ranks.

A cell is capacity-limited if the whole requested batch cannot remain resident with allocation headroom. Such cells are not silently converted to smaller queued batches. Each timing submits one request wave at the requested concurrency and includes its natural completion tail. Validation checks output count, prompt/output lengths, retractions, graph replay, and the full requested batch in the profiled initial decode iterations on both ranks. Cold latency, timing range, acceptance, and profiled GPU-step duration are retained in the machine-readable results.

The new experimental schedule partitions the captured verification-A and independent draft-B graphs at communication boundaries, subdivides draft compute into smaller node groups, and distributes those groups across opposite-phase target windows. A single flat CUDA graph uses GPU fork/join dependencies to prevent communication/communication and compute/compute overlap. Draft communication remains ordered with draft compute. Kernel launch attributes are copied, and dependencies are conservatively strengthened to completion fences.

This change covers the independent draft-B / verification-A pair. Draft-A, both draft extensions, and verification-B retain their existing dependencies, including the extension-A / verification-B fence. Consequently, the paired-graph overlap percentage is not the fraction of all draft work hidden over the complete decoding step. Fences may also lengthen target windows; actual kernel intersections and unprofiled end-to-end throughput must both be examined.

The benchmark provides a serialized version of the same composed graph and the previous whole-graph launch schedule as controls. CUPTI clone identities attribute kernels inside the joint graph to their source model. Separate graph launches are attributed through CPU scopes and CUPTI correlation IDs. Overlap percentages use kernel interval unions, and forbidden-overlap checks use the maximum over all captured cycles on both ranks.

Code checkpoint: a74d7893ca — phase-fenced speculative CUDA graph interleaving and EP2 profiling. Pre-commit checks and 42 unit tests passed. The two-rank synthetic checks cover exact graph-output equivalence and preservation of nondefault kernel attributes. Completed experiment tables, token checks, and raw evidence follow below.
